newsitem.title: USA: Boeing doubles income, revenue on higher sales.
newsitem.headline: Boeing doubles income, revenue on higher sales.

text.p: Boeing Co. said Monday its first-quarter profit more than doubled and its sales grew by 70 percent, reflecting a rise in the number of aircraft delivered and the company's acquisition of Rockwell International Corp.'s defence and aerospace businesses.
Boeing said it earned $313 million, or 87 cents a share, on revenue of $7.32 billion in the period ended March 31.

A year earlier, the company earned $119 million, or 35 cents a share, on revenue of $4.29 billion. Boeing also recorded income of $64 million related to an accounting change at an employee-benefit trust fund.

Boeing said it delivered a total of 68 aircraft during the quarter, up from 40 in the year-earlier quarter. Boeing noted that shipments in the year-earlier period were reduced as a result of a strike in the fourth quarter of 1995.
The world's largest commercial aircraft maker, Boeing said it expected to deliver 90 aircraft during the current quarter.
The company also said it expected the world's airlines to take delivery of $1.1 trillion worth of new aircraft over the next 20 years.

Partially offsetting the increase in Boeing's income were higher research and development expense for the commercial aircraft and defence and space segments, increased interest expense from the Rockwell acquisition, development expenses related to two joint ventures, and a higher income tax rate.
Boeing completed the acquisition of Rockwell's defence and aerospace units in December.
Boeing's stock, which closed Friday at $102 on the New York Stock Exchange , did not immediately begin trading when the market opened Monday.
